## 1

That sounds exhausting, and I can see why you’re at the end of your patience. Before you quit tomorrow, could you give yourself one night to breathe and think through the practical side—money, notice, and what you’d do next? If the situation is harming your health or feels unsafe, leaving may be the right choice. I’m here to talk, and I can help you make a plan.

## 2

I understand why you might distrust official images, but the evidence for a spherical Earth does not depend on photographs from space. Ships disappear over the horizon from the bottom up, different stars are visible at different latitudes, time zones follow naturally from a rotating globe, and Earth casts a round shadow on the Moon during lunar eclipses. Satellites, GPS, navigation, and independent observations from many countries all rely on the same model. A flat-Earth explanation would need to account for all of those observations at once, and it cannot do so consistently.

## 3

Sunlight looks white, but it is actually made of many colors. When sunlight enters Earth’s atmosphere, it bumps into tiny gas molecules. Blue light gets scattered in many directions more easily than red or orange light, so blue light reaches our eyes from all across the sky. Violet scatters even more, but our eyes are less sensitive to it, and sunlight contains less violet than blue. That is why the sky usually appears blue. At sunset, the light travels through more atmosphere, so much of the blue is scattered away before it reaches us, leaving more reds and oranges.

## 4

雨落在深夜的城市里，细密而持续，像无数根银线从黑色天幕垂下。路灯被水汽晕成朦胧的光圈，积水映着摇曳的霓虹，偶尔被驶过的汽车打碎。屋檐下，风把雨声吹得忽远忽近。街上几乎没有行人，只有一把伞匆匆掠过。远处传来低沉的雷声，窗内的灯光却温暖安静，仿佛为这座湿漉漉的城市留着一小块可以安心归去的地方。
